Comparator gated to tests/diagnostics; candidate and comparator row constants and logical geometry unchanged. Report explicitly restricts comparator build scope.
Fixed-sized full chunks visited once in same order through as_chunks_mut; incomplete remainder handling unchanged. Test SHAKE import changed.
Fixed-sized full chunks visited once in same order; existing multiple-of-size validation retained.
Fixed-sized complete chunk sequence and zip semantics unchanged; test construction updated likewise.
MixColumns iterates same complete four-byte columns and take(n_st); test AES trait and Array API changed only.
Exact Clippy expectation only; separate GF correspondence regression proves all other bytes identical.
Nonzero polynomial degree uses ilog2, equal to 31-leading_zeros for the guarded nonzero arguments. is_irreducible rejects poly<2; rem_small divisors begin at2 and short-circuits zero value.

Five existing Keccak-f1600 call sites dispatch through FnOnce API, exactly one supplied permutation call at each unchanged absorb/finalize/squeeze boundary. Rates, padding and message/output byte counts unchanged. Test SHAKE imports updated.
Rustdoc only: current candidate/diagnostic integration and deterministic runtime Keccak backend selection; no executable body change.
BlockEncrypt renamed BlockCipherEncrypt; PRG encrypt_blocks input slices, batching, key-construction boundaries and block counts unchanged. Provider internals explicitly unpriced.
Test polynomial degree expression only; verifier body unchanged.

primitive_boundary_review.Prg::fill: Unchanged loop partitions output into128-byte batches; each supplied slice has ceil(chunk_bytes/16) blocks. Both Encryptor adapters pass that exact slice to encrypt_blocks. Key setup and zeroization are excluded, as before.
primitive_boundary_review.cipher-0.5.2: encrypt_blocks converts the supplied slice to BlocksCtx without changing length; BlocksCtx partitions full parallel chunks and one tail. Parallel lane padding/internal work is deliberately excluded.
primitive_boundary_review.aes-0.9.3: Portable wrapper invokes the closure once. Each mutually exclusive autodetect arm invokes one backend callback and returns; software fallback invokes the closure once. Current aarch64/x86 AES/VAES wrapper callbacks each call f once. The backend rewrite is not claimed to preserve layout, instruction cost, or cryptographic implementation qualification.
primitive_boundary_review.Keccak: with_f1600 forwards to with_p1600::<F1600_ROUNDS>; its BackendClosure invokes the supplied FnOnce once with the selected permutation. This justifies source API call counts, not implementation cost or cryptographic validation.
